Name: overthinking_verification_loop_circuit
Title: Circuits of Doubt: Attention Heads That Trigger Redundant Self-Verification
Short Hypothesis: Overthinking (excessive re-verification producing tokens like 'wait, let me check again') is driven by a small, identifiable set of attention heads that detect local uncertainty and initiate verification loops. Ablating or dampening these heads reduces trace length with minimal accuracy cost on easy problems.
Related Work: Chen et al. (2024) 'Do NOT Think That Much' document overthinking behaviorally; Olsson et al. (2022) induction heads; Wang et al. (2023) label-word attention. We move from behavior to circuit: we localize the specific heads that gate verification onset and demonstrate causal control, distinguishing productive verification (hard problems) from reflexive loops (easy problems).
Abstract: Reasoning models often re-verify already-correct conclusions, inflating cost. We hypothesize that verification onset is mediated by a sparse set of attention heads acting as uncertainty detectors that write a 'reconsider' signal into the residual stream, triggering backtracking phrases. We localize these heads by (i) contrasting head activations at tokens immediately preceding verification phrases versus matched control tokens, and (ii) path-patching from these heads to the logits of trigger tokens ('wait', 'but', 'let me recheck'). We then perform graded head interventions-scaling attention output-and measure effects on verification frequency, trace length, and final accuracy, separately for easy and hard problems. We predict a dissociation: dampening the heads shortens easy-problem traces without accuracy loss but harms hard problems where verification is warranted, revealing that the same circuit serves both adaptive and maladaptive verification. We further test whether a problem-difficulty feature upstream modulates these heads, suggesting overthinking is a mis-calibration of an otherwise useful circuit. The work yields a mechanistic account of overthinking and a targeted, interpretable knob for efficient reasoning that outperforms blanket length penalties.
Experiments: 1. Detect verification-trigger tokens via lexical + classifier tagging in R1-Distill traces on GSM8K (easy) and MATH-hard. 2. For each head, compute activation difference at pre-trigger vs control positions; rank heads. 3. Path-patch top heads to trigger-token logits to confirm causal role. 4. Graded intervention: scale top-k head outputs by beta in {0,0.25,0.5,1}; measure verification count, tokens, accuracy, split by difficulty. 5. Test upstream difficulty feature: probe for difficulty, correlate with head activation. 6. Compare efficiency (tokens saved at fixed accuracy) against length-penalty RL and prompt-based 'be concise' baselines.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Verification tagging is imperfect and lexically biased across languages. Heads may be polysemantic; ablation could damage unrelated capabilities. The easy/hard dissociation may be graded rather than clean. Interventions may generalize poorly to models trained with different RL recipes.
